L1.definition: NO when a semantic-conservative OldBasis -> NewRepresentation mapping preserves states, operations and questions
L1.evidence: the complete compile-away mapping does not preserve every transition question or falsifier

L2.definition: YES only for a previously unproducible object/operator class
L2.evidence: first-class transition relation and binding constraint are not represented as one local object

L3.definition: YES only with a pre-leap unaskable to post-leap representable question
L3.evidence: Q2-Q6 become representable in MT while MS remains endpoint/local only

L4.definition: YES only for a failure mode passing all old checks
L4.evidence: 120 fresh endpoint-valid holdout instances fail MT while all old checks pass

L5.definition: supportive only; requires two independent pre-existing families

L6.definition: YES only if removing the new semantic primitive loses capability
L6.evidence: transition ablations lose detections and compile-away is not complete

challenger_priority.definition: any complete challenger plus no independent L2/L3/L4/L6 increment is NON_LEAP
